20th Century Girl

20세기 소녀

K-Drama · Movie · South Korea · 2022

⭐☆☆☆☆1B/10

Overview

Set in 1999, 20th Century Girl tells the story of Na Bo-ra, a cheerful seventeen-year-old high school student and Taekwondo practitioner. Before leaving for the United States for heart surgery, her best friend, Kim Yeon-du, asks Bo-ra to secretly observe and gather information about the boy she has a crush on, Baek Hyun-jin. To fulfill her promise, Bo-ra joins the school's broadcasting club, where she unexpectedly becomes close to Hyun-jin's best friend, Poong Woon-ho. As they spend more time together, Bo-ra slowly falls in love with him. However, she later discovers that Yeon-du had mistaken the identity of her crush—it was actually Woon-ho all along. Choosing her friendship over her own happiness, Bo-ra hides her feelings. Before Woon-ho returns to New Zealand, the two finally confess their love for one another and promise to meet again. But after his departure, Woon-ho suddenly stops replying to Bo-ra's emails without explanation. Years later, Bo-ra receives an invitation to an art exhibition from Woon-ho's younger brother, Joseph. There, she learns the heartbreaking truth that Woon-ho had passed away years earlier in an accident. The exhibition contains the artwork and memories he left behind, including a video he made for Bo-ra, allowing her to finally understand what happened and say goodbye to her first love.

My Review

This movie completely broke me. At first, I thought it would just be another nostalgic high school romance, but it became one of the saddest first-love stories I've ever watched. The chemistry between Bo-ra and Woon-ho felt so genuine. Their little interactions, teasing, and innocent love made me smile throughout the movie. It never felt forced—it felt real. Then the ending happened. I kept waiting for Woon-ho to come back. I thought there would be a reason why he suddenly stopped replying to Bo-ra's emails. I kept believing they would meet again someday. Instead, I learned the truth together with Bo-ra. The scene at the art exhibition completely shattered me. Watching the video Woon-ho left behind made me cry because it showed that every single moment they spent together was precious to him. Bo-ra never got the chance to properly say goodbye, and neither did we. This movie perfectly captures how beautiful, innocent, and painful first love can be. Some people stay in your heart forever, even if fate doesn't allow you to stay together.

Favorite Scene/Part

• The train station scene where Bo-ra and Woon-ho finally confess their feelings before he leaves for New Zealand. • The final art exhibition scene where Bo-ra watches Woon-ho's recorded video and relives every beautiful memory they shared.

Favorite Quote/Lines

"I like you, Na Bo-ra."
